uncertainty: Training variability was summarized by five-seed standard deviations, pointwise 95\% Student-$t$ intervals with four degrees of freedom and counts of seeds with a positive removal effect. These seed-based summaries describe variability across five fitted models, whereas the bootstrap intervals describe test-sample uncertainty conditional on those models; neither combines all sources of uncertainty. All reported confidence intervals are pointwise 95\%, without family-wise or false-discovery-rate adjustment. For ablation, test-sample uncertainty was estimated using paired moving blocks of 28 consecutive six-hourly samples (seven days), with 10,000 replicates and resampling seed 42 specified in the archived analysis code. The same sampled blocks were used for the full and reduced configurations and across seeds; RMSE differences were calculated within each seed and then averaged, rather than first averaging predictions across seeds. For SHAP, sampling intervals used 2,000 bootstrap replicates resampling explained cases by calendar day, with resampling seed 42 specified in the code; the fixed background was not resampled. These intervals address test-case sampling uncertainty and do not evaluate sensitivity to alternative backgrounds.
negative: The BU-LSTM-Attention results were less stable across training seeds. Removing tcc or sp increased RMSE in four of five seeds; their pointwise 95\% moving-block bootstrap intervals excluded zero, but their seed-$t$ intervals included zero. They are therefore not described as equally robust to the BiLSTM-Attention effects. Removing individual precipitation-related predictors sometimes improved performance; for mntpr, the overall mean difference was negative and both pointwise intervals excluded zero. Overall ablation-rank agreement across seeds was 0.867 for BiLSTM-Attention and 0.543 for BU-LSTM-Attention, further indicating architecture-dependent training variability.
